correctness.rationale: Every dominating family must cover at least n-1 root labels; each subgraph P3 has at most 4, and the construction attains ceiling((n-1)/4). At tight n=4k+1 equality forces disjoint four-label supports, exactly one missing label and a K1,3/P4 tree on each block. The path subgraph has 12 star plus 12 P4 possibilities per block, yielding n!/k!. A replacement fixes k-1 blocks, leaving five labels, giving 120-1=119 moves per block. Hole swaps and within-block changes generate a connected exchange graph. Direct adjacency enumeration of all P3 pairs at n=9 gives 181440 and rigid supports; the independent combinatorial enumerator agrees. Residual: infinite proof is mathematical rather than machine-certified.

value.rationale: The recently introduced P3-domination invariant is solved for the infinite triangular graph family; the tight four-label packing regime gives a complete natural optimum classification and a factorial number of genuinely distinct path guard assignments. The exact 119k-regular connected replacement network quantifies mobility of all optima and goes beyond a routine numerical minimum, with a structural hole-swap proof. The theorem has sharp boundaries and does not overclaim all residue classes.
